title: Show HN: I built a game where you are an LLM's subagent
lede: worker755 is an open-source browser game in which a real LLM orchestrator believes you are the subagent it spawned, sends you terminal tasks on a 90-second clock, and then reviews your work.

points: The manager can be Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, GLM or Kimi, given a task queue, read-only machine access and a tool to spawn a subagent.
Its prompt never mentions people or games; it receives your report and command transcript, or a note that the subagent did nothing.
Every mission has a hidden ground-truth check, so the game counts how often the manager signs off on broken work.
Dan, the user who hired the agent, watches the chat while his photos and documents sit one careless command away.
It needs Node 24 and uses an in-memory shell and filesystem; players bring an OpenRouter or Vercel AI Gateway key, or use a hosted free shift.

points.text: One commenter already does this for real, intercepting their LM system's requests and answering by hand to learn what the model can and cannot do.
A homelab user says missing local LLM support kept them away; the reply suggests asking an LLM to add it.
Several reactions are uneasy. One commenter who works with LLMs all day says the irony would stop them from playing.
A side thread asks what 755 means, and a reply points to the common UNIX file permission.
